newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Oscar winners to make film about Britain's RAF.
newsitem.headline: Czech Oscar winners to make film about Britain's RAF.

text.p: The Czech father and son film-making team of Zdenek and Jan Sverak, who made "Kolya", this Oscar winner for the best foreign language film, have chosen a tale about Czechs serving in Britain's Royal Air Force for their next project.
The Czech daily Mlada Fronta Dnes quoted the son, 32-year-old director Jan, as saying his father was working on a script for a World War Two story which would not be a "pure" comedy.
The title, cast and schedule are still a heavily-guarded secret.
The grey-bearded Zdenek is writing the script in Czech but it will be filmed in English, marking the successful pair's first attempt at an original English-language project.

The bittersweet "Kolya", about an old bachelor stuck with an abandoned Russian boy on the eve of Prague's 1989 Velvet Revolution, was distributed by Miramax, backers of "The English Patient" which won the this year's Oscar for Best Picture.

This time the Sverak team agreed with Miramax to try their hand at an English-language film which they said would open their quirky and touching work to a wider audience and maybe allow them a shot at a "Best Picture" Oscar.
